Hello,

I have strong opinions about simplicity. Not "let's make it pretty" simplicity—the kind where you remove everything that doesn't serve the user until only the essential remains.

Your job description mentions "prefers simplicity over complexity." That's not just a preference for me—it's a philosophy I've built my career around. At CREATE SOMETHING, we call it the Subtractive Triad: eliminate duplication, eliminate excess, eliminate disconnection. The best interfaces reveal what users need by removing what they don't.

I noticed Centaur builds data labeling tools—interfaces where users need to "tackle complex problems" with "just enough information while inviting the user to learn more." That's the exact tension I've spent 12 years navigating: how do you make complex workflows feel simple without hiding essential complexity?

Opinions about design, copy, and UI/UX I'm UI/UX certified and spent two years as an On-Screen Educator at Webflow, teaching thousands of users how to build. That work forces you to develop strong opinions about what makes interfaces intuitive—because you see exactly where people get stuck.
Streamlined workflows for large datasets At Webflow, I built tools for managing a marketplace with thousands of templates. Upload workflows, async processing, progress feedback, filtering complex datasets—I've solved these problems in production.
Balance quality with speed, refactor as you go I run two startups alongside my day job. I know when to ship fast and when to slow down. The trick is building systems that let you do both—clean enough to refactor, fast enough to learn.
Backend experience Node.js, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, data pipelines. I'm comfortable across the stack—which matters when you're integrating frontend with backend systems.
CST timezone, ready to collaborate I'm in Texas (CST), which aligns with your timezone preference. I've worked with distributed teams at Webflow and on my own projects.

I'm genuinely excited about Centaur's problem space. Data labeling tools are where interface design really matters—every unnecessary click, every confusing label, every slow interaction compounds into frustration or efficiency. Getting that right is craft work.

I'd welcome the chance to discuss how my experience building intuitive interfaces for complex problems could contribute to Centaur's product.
